entries.name: Flip an object over
entries.line: Turns an object over to its other side with a small overshoot, starting from wherever it is; call it again to turn it back.
entries.use_for: a question turning into its answer; a change of mind; an answer turning over to show it is wrong; the other side of a card; something that turns over

call.signature: PCS.flip(layer, { t, dur, axis, dir })

options.name: t
options.text: start time in seconds (required)

options.name: dur
options.text: length in seconds, default 0.42 (the overshoot peaks at 72 percent)

options.name: axis
options.text: 'y' turns like a page (default); 'x' tips over like a tile

options.name: dir
options.text: 1 or -1, which way it turns

notes: put what the back says on the back face before the flip, the right way up for the axis it turns on.

entries.name: Hand over from a face card beat to a cutaway room
entries.line: In one comp with one camera, turns a face card beat into a full-frame cutaway: the face card slides away, the dark backplate falls away to reveal a lit room, the stage's light gives way to the room's, the camera travels from the face-on view down into the room, and the object that carried the idea flies into the room and lands where it belongs.
entries.use_for: the moment the explanation leaves the speaker for a cutaway; continuity between a face card beat and the cutaway after it; a carried object from the previous beat flying into the room

call.signature: PCS.handOver(st, { t, dur, carry, to, pose, leave })

options.name: st
options.text: what PCS.stage returned (the beat's comp, its backplate, its lights and its camera)

options.name: t
options.text: when the hand-over starts (required)

options.name: dur
options.text: seconds, default 1.0

options.name: carry
options.text: the layer that carries the idea into the room (optional); it keeps its colour and flies in an arc

options.name: to
options.text: where carry lands, [x, y, z] in the room (rm.stand(h, x, z) or rm.lie(x, z, depth) give a spot on the floor)

options.name: pose
options.text: carry's [x, y] rotation on landing, default [0, -12]

options.name: leave
options.text: layers that are finished; each tips away into the dark as the room arrives

call.returns: what PCS.room returns, for the room's floor, lights and spots
notes: nothing cuts: one comp, one camera, and the carried object stays in view the whole way. The accent stays on it.
the stage's key and fill are renamed 'stage key' and 'stage fill' and fade out; 'key' is the room's from then on.
what is finished leaves in the same half second as the room arrives; never fade or grey it out.

entries.name: Show or hide an object with what sits on it
entries.line: Makes an object, and everything seated on it, appear at one time (hideUntil) or vanish at one time (hideAfter), with a clean cut and no fade.
entries.use_for: an object that arrives with its move; one that leaves after its move; keeping type off screen until its card has turned to face us

call.signature: PCS.hideUntil(layer, t)  and  PCS.hideAfter(layer, t)

options.name: t
options.text: the time it appears (hideUntil) or goes (hideAfter)

notes: on a light it sets the light's start (hideUntil) or end (hideAfter); a pool made with piece-spot's on already goes with its object.
children do not take a parent's opacity in After Effects, so hiding a plate by its own opacity leaves its labels floating; this hides them all.
never fade or grey something out to dismiss it; move it away (piece-tip-away) and hide it once it is gone.

entries.name: Flat crisp label
entries.line: Sets one line of flat type in the style's font, in the colour that reads on what it sits on (the ground, a surface or the accent), unlit so it keeps its exact colour.
entries.use_for: what a card says; a caption under a number; a short supporting line beside a lit object

call.signature: PCS.label(comp, { text, size, weight, color, on, maxWidth, anchor, pos, name })

options.name: text
options.text: the words

options.name: size
options.text: pixels, default 64; never under 44 on a phone frame

options.name: on
options.text: 'ground' (default), 'surface' or 'accent': picks the style colour that reads there

options.name: color
options.text: overrides on

options.name: maxWidth
options.text: shrinks the size until the line fits this width

options.name: anchor
options.text: 'left' sets the anchor at the line's left edge (default its centre)

options.name: pos
options.text: [x, y, z]

call.example:
var card = PCS.plate(st.comp, { name: 'card', w: 720, h: 300, round: 34, pos: [540, 600, 0] });
PCS.onFace(PCS.label(st.comp, { text: '42 passed, 0 failed', size: 60, on: 'surface' }), card);
notes: type on a plate is flat, never extruded; one hero word that should be an object is piece-type3d.

entries.name: Carry an object onto another
entries.line: One object travels in an arc toward the camera and seats itself on a plate's face, taking the plate's angle, with a small settle; it can shrink as it lands.
entries.use_for: a seal or stamp on a result (a stamp of approval); a piece fitting into place; a carried object from the previous beat arriving on the next thing; the thing that carried one idea arriving on the next

call.signature: PCS.landOn(obj, plate, { at, t, dur, lift, scale, gap })

options.name: at
options.text: [x, y] on the plate's face from its centre, default [0, 0]

options.name: t
options.text: when it leaves (required)

options.name: dur
options.text: seconds, default 0.5

options.name: lift
options.text: how far toward the camera it comes on the way, default 260, so it never cuts through the plate

options.name: scale
options.text: its size in percent at landing, absolute (100 is its own size, whatever scale it had before), with a small overshoot; left out, it keeps its size

options.name: gap
options.text: space in front of the face, default 4

call.returns: where it lands, [x, y, z] in the comp
call.example:
PCS.standUp(card, { t: 2.6 });
PCS.landOn(tile.front, card, { at: [250, 130], t: 3.3, dur: 0.6, scale: 34 });
notes: it lands where the plate is when it lands and does not follow it afterwards, so the plate's own move must be over by the time the landing ends (it warns if not). The landing may start while the plate is still standing up: piece-stand-up pivots on the plate's bottom edge, so it never sweeps through an object coming in front of it.
it keeps whichever side is showing; a flip still running when it leaves is finished on the way, so it lands on the side the flip was turning to. A flip timed to start after it leaves is dropped.
a stamp or seal on a result: land the tick tile on the card, scale about 50, lift 400 or more.

entries.name: Move or grow an object to a new place
entries.line: Takes an object from wherever it is at a time to a new resting place, a new size, or both, eased, with an optional overshoot; it chains with the other moves on the same object (a flip, a stand-up, a landing), and its pool of light follows it and grows with it.
entries.use_for: an object growing and coming forward to become the hero; a carried object from the previous beat moving to its new place; a tile rising into the question while it turns over; making room for what comes next

call.signature: PCS.move(layer, { t, dur, to, by, scale, overshoot })

options.name: t
options.text: when it starts (required)

options.name: dur
options.text: seconds, default 0.5

options.name: to
options.text: [x, y] or [x, y, z], where it comes to rest (its position: in the comp, or in its parent's space if it has one); a missing z keeps its depth

options.name: by
options.text: [dx, dy] or [dx, dy, dz] instead of to: how far it moves from where it is at t

options.name: scale
options.text: its size in percent at rest, absolute (100 is its own size, whatever scale it had before); a number, or [x, y]

options.name: overshoot
options.text: percent of the move it goes past before settling back, default 0 (a plain ease); 6 to 10 gives a small bounce

notes: moves chain in time order: each one starts from where the object is at its t and drops any keys of the same kind after its t, so add an object's moves from first to last.
on a two-sided object move its front; the back follows it. Start a move after a stand-up has settled.
rendered positions differ from comp positions (the camera sits low and left): check where it lands with a render or PCS.onScreen.

entries.name: Seat a layer on a face of an object
entries.line: Puts a layer (type, a tick, a picture, a smaller plate) on the front or the back face of a plate, so it moves, turns and stands up with it.
entries.use_for: words or a mark on a card, a pill or a tile; what the back says before a flip; a raised detail on a face

call.signature: PCS.onFace(layer, plate, at, lit)  and  PCS.onBack(layer, plate, at, axis, gap)

options.name: at
options.text: [x, y] from the plate's centre, default [0, 0]

options.name: lit
options.text: onFace only. false (default) keeps flat graphics and type their exact colour; true seats a thick detail (a smaller plate) that takes the light

options.name: axis
options.text: onBack only. The axis the plate will flip on ('x' or 'y'), so the back reads the right way up after the flip

options.name: gap
options.text: onBack only. Distance behind the plate's body, default twice the bevel plus 6

notes: children do not take a parent's opacity in After Effects: hide an object with piece-hide, which takes what sits on it too.

entries.name: A picture or screenshot as the face of an object
entries.line: Puts a picture, a screenshot, a movie or a comp on a plate's front face, filled to the face inside a small rim and cut to its rounded corners, so the screen is part of a lit object rather than a flat card.
entries.use_for: a real screen or app shown as a device; a document page; a photo on a card; the product itself

call.signature: PCS.pictureFace(plate, { source, inset, fit, lit, name })

options.name: source
options.text: a project item (footage or comp) or a file path (imported once)

options.name: inset
options.text: the rim of plate left showing around the picture, default 18

options.name: fit
options.text: 'cover' (default) fills the face and trims the overflow; 'contain' shows the whole picture

options.name: lit
options.text: false (default) keeps the picture's own colours, like a screen; true lets the stage's lights fall on it, like a print

call.returns: the picture layer, seated on the plate (it moves, turns and stands up with it)
call.example:
var tablet = PCS.plate(st.comp, { name: 'tablet', w: 820, h: 560, round: 44, pos: [540, 600, 0] });
PCS.pictureFace(tablet, { source: 'screenshots/app.png' });
notes: the plate's own colour shows as the rim: a dark surface reads as a device, the accent as a frame.
set the plate a little larger than the picture's shape; a cover fit trims what does not fit the face.

entries.name: Thick lit plate
entries.line: Makes one thick, bevelled slab that takes the light and casts a shadow: a card, a pill, a tile, a chip or a bar.
entries.use_for: anything that should look built rather than drawn; the object words and pictures sit on (a card, a document, a receipt, a tile, a pill)

call.signature: PCS.plate(comp, { name, w, h, round, color, depth, bevel, pos, tilt })

options.name: w, h
options.text: size in pixels

options.name: round
options.text: corner radius; h / 2 makes a pill

options.name: color
options.text: default the style's surface colour

options.name: depth
options.text: thickness, default the style's depth

options.name: bevel
options.text: edge bevel, 0 for none; default the style's bevel

options.name: pos
options.text: [x, y, z]

options.name: tilt
options.text: [x, y] resting angle in degrees; default the style's tilt, which shows the side wall and the bottom edge

call.returns: the plate layer (its front face at local z 0; the body runs back to z = depth)
call.example:
var st = PCS.stage({ name: 'BEAT 3', duration: 5 });
var pill = PCS.plate(st.comp, { name: 'pill', w: 780, h: 160, round: 80, pos: [540, 300, 0] });
notes: two equal plates on screen means no hero; make one bigger, nearer or in the pool of light.

entries.name: Lit room for a full-frame cutaway
entries.line: Makes the full-frame setting for a cutaway: a floor and a back wall, a key that casts shadows, a front fill, a cool wash on the wall and a two-node camera looking down into the room that pushes in slowly with depth of field, all coloured by the style.
entries.use_for: a cutaway beat where objects stand or lie in a place (documents on a floor, a device on a desk, chosen items standing up); never behind the speaker's face card

call.signature: PCS.room({ name, duration, comp, t, dur, cam })

options.name: name, duration
options.text: a new comp's name and length in seconds

options.name: comp
options.text: build the room inside this comp instead (piece-hand-over does this); its lights then rise from 0 at t over dur

options.name: t, dur
options.text: with comp, when the room's lights come up (default 0) and over how long (0.8)

options.name: cam
options.text: with comp, the camera to take over from t; without it a new camera named 'cam' is made

options.name: camDur
options.text: with cam, how long the camera takes to reach the room's view, default dur

call.returns: { comp, floor, wall, key, fill, wash, env, cam, floorY, stand(h, x, z), lie(x, z, depth) }
notes: colours come from the style: its wall and floor values when it has them, else the wall from its backplate and quiet colour and the floor from its backplate and surface. The wash takes its wash colour, else its fill colour.
rm.stand(h, x, z) is the position for an upright plate h tall standing on the floor at x, z; rm.lie(x, z, depth) for one lying flat, face up (give it tilt [-90, 0]).
a pool on something in the room comes from above (piece-spot with from: 'above'), so it also lights the floor around it; from the front it would splash the wall.
the light picture is set for a 1080 x 1920 frame with the camera's own framing; objects read best between z 300 and 1600 on the floor.

entries.name: Raised rows of content on a card
entries.line: Lays thin lit bars on a plate's face as lines of a log, a list or a document, each growing in from the left in turn, with an optional tick before each.
entries.use_for: evidence on a card: a test log, a checklist, a receipt, a document, a list that fills as it is read

call.signature: PCS.rows(comp, plate, { n, widths, left, top, rowWidth, h, gap, color, ticks, t, stagger })

options.name: n
options.text: how many rows, default 3

options.name: widths
options.text: each row's share of rowWidth (0 to 1), default [0.86, 0.62, 0.94, 0.5, 0.78, 0.7], repeating

options.name: left, top
options.text: where the first row starts, from the plate's centre (default left = -rowWidth / 2, top = 0: the first row on the plate's middle line, the rest below it)

options.name: rowWidth
options.text: the longest row's width, default 70 percent of the plate's width; with ticks, the rows start 2.2 x h to the right of left, after the tick

options.name: h, gap
options.text: row height, default 22, and the space between rows, default 34, so row i sits at top + i x (h + gap) and n rows take n x h + (n - 1) x gap

options.name: color
options.text: default a tone between the style's surface and ink

options.name: ticks
options.text: true puts a small tick before each row

options.name: t, stagger
options.text: the first row grows in at t, the next one stagger seconds later (default 0.09); each row grows from its left over 0.22 s and its tick pops in with it, so the last row is in at t + (n - 1) x stagger + 0.22; without t all show from the start

call.example:
var card = PCS.plate(st.comp, { name: 'card', w: 720, h: 470, round: 34, pos: [540, 900, 0] });
PCS.rows(st.comp, card, { n: 3, left: -300, top: -150, rowWidth: 430, ticks: true, t: 3.1 });

entries.name: Spot light, or a pool of light on the hero
entries.line: Adds one spot light coloured by the style. Given an object (on), it lights that object from in front, up and to one side, with a pool sized to it that follows the object wherever it moves and goes out when the object is hidden or tips away; it can rise as the object arrives while the stage's key dips, so the lit thing is the one to look at.
entries.use_for: the one thing the line is about ("the light tells the story"); a light that keeps rising on a held picture; the key and fill of a stage

call.signature: PCS.spot(comp, { name, on, from, t, dur, dimKey, pos, aim, color, intensity, cone, feather, shadow, darkness, diffusion })

options.name: on
options.text: a layer to light: aims at its centre from in front, up and to the left, cone sized to it, feather 75. The light follows the layer (moves added before or after are both followed) and its pool grows and shrinks with it, is off while the layer is hidden or out of its time, and in front its light stops just past the object, so no pool is left on the wall behind

options.name: from
options.text: with on, 'front' (default, for a face card stage) or 'above' (for a room: high above, so the pool also falls on the floor around it)

options.name: t, dur
options.text: the pool rises from 0 at t over dur seconds (default 0.8); without t it is on from the start. A long dur (3 or more) is a light that keeps rising, which keeps a held picture alive

options.name: dimKey
options.text: 0 to 1, the stage's key and fill fall to this share of their strength over the same time (0.6 makes the pool read twice as strong)

options.name: intensity
options.text: percent; with on, by how light the object is and how much light already reaches it: 1.0 x the style's key plus fill on a dark object, down to 0.5 x on a near-white or fully saturated one, so a pool reads on graphite and never clips cream; else 80

options.name: pos, aim
options.text: [x, y, z] where the light sits and the point it points at (without on)

options.name: cone, feather
options.text: cone angle in degrees (default 80, or sized to the object with on) and feather percent (90, or 75 with on)

options.name: color
options.text: default the style's key colour

options.name: shadow
options.text: true to cast shadows (darkness 60, diffusion 90 unless given)

notes: one pool, on the one hero. Light it from the front but off the camera's line: from high above a pool only grazes a face and lights the wall behind; straight from the camera it puts a milky highlight over a glossy face and washes what is on it.
hiding or tipping the object away takes its pool with it; to end a pool by itself, PCS.hideAfter(light, t).
never a point light near a glossy surface (it shows as a stray dot).

entries.name: Lit stage for a face card beat
entries.line: Makes a vertical Advanced 3D comp with a dark ground, a backplate that catches light and shadow, a key with soft shadows, a fill, a slowly drifting camera and grain on the graphics only, all coloured by the style.
entries.use_for: every face card beat that puts lit 3D graphics above the speaker; a held picture that keeps moving (its camera drifts slowly for the whole comp)

call.signature: PCS.stage({ name, duration, env, stitch, replace })

options.name: name
options.text: the new comp's name

options.name: duration
options.text: seconds

options.name: env
options.text: path to an environment light map (.hdr); default assets/studio-strips.hdr beside the pieces when it is there, else no environment light

options.name: stitch
options.text: { path, start } puts the speaker's clip in a rounded card at the bottom, starting at that time in the clip

options.name: replace
options.text: true rebuilds the comp in its place: an earlier comp of this name is removed first, with its solids, nulls and the light map it brought in (footage from elsewhere, such as the speaker's clip, stays), and the new one goes in the same folder; for look-and-fix rounds. It refuses a comp used inside another

call.returns: { comp, backplate, key, fill, cam, grain, warnings }
call.example:
PCS.use('example-warm-paper');
var st = PCS.stage({ name: 'BEAT 3', duration: 5, replace: true });
notes: 2D layers (grain, the face card) stay on top; pieces seat new 3D layers under them by themselves.

read before placing anything. Graphics live on screen in y 220 to 1180, above the speaker's card (its top edge is at screen y 1360); fill that area: no more than about a fifth of it empty, so make objects big.
one hero per picture: bigger, nearer, or in the pool of light (piece-spot). Two equal plates means no hero.

those numbers are on screen; the positions you give are the comp's, and the camera (low, left of centre, drifting) shows an object at depth 0 higher than its comp y: about 50 px in the lower half and 60 to 80 px near the top. So screen y 220 to 1180 is comp y about 285 to 1230 at depth 0. Objects also lean differently at the top and bottom. Check a placing with PCS.onScreen(layer, null, t), which gives [x, y] on screen, or a render, not by arithmetic.
type on a plate is flat (piece-label); only a hero word is an object (piece-type3d). Move things off with piece-tip-away, never a fade.
the camera's slow drift keeps a held picture alive by itself; a pool that keeps rising (piece-spot, long dur) adds to it. No other motion is needed to hold.

entries.name: Stand an object up
entries.line: An object (a plate, a card, a two-sided tile's front or a hero word from piece-type3d) lying flat on its back stands up on its bottom edge, past upright, and settles back, from wherever its rotation is; what sits on it stays hidden until it is half way up, so no type is seen squashed edge-on.
entries.use_for: a pill, a card or a result arriving by standing up; a big word (piece-type3d) arriving; the one item chosen from many standing up to be seen

call.signature: PCS.standUp(layer, { t, dur, hide, hinge })

options.name: t
options.text: when it starts (required)

options.name: dur
options.text: seconds, default 0.5 (past upright at 60 percent, settled at the end)

options.name: hide
options.text: false keeps it visible before t (default: hidden until t)

options.name: hinge
options.text: 'bottom' (default) pivots on its bottom edge (for type, the bottom of its letters' box), as a thing standing up does: it lies back away from the camera and never sweeps through what is in front of or below it; 'centre' turns about its middle. Once it has settled it turns about its middle again, so later flips stay in place

notes: seated layers with their own opacity timing keep it.
an object can land on it while it stands (piece-land-on) as long as the landing ends after it has settled.

entries.name: Change what a face says while it is turned away
entries.line: At one moment the old layer on a face goes and the new one shows, so an object that turns away and back comes back saying something new.
entries.use_for: a card that turns twice and returns with a new message; a counter that changes while edge-on; a third side on a two-sided object

call.signature: PCS.swapFace(oldLayer, newLayer, t)

options.name: t
options.text: the swap time; put it where the face is edge-on or turned away (half way through a flip)

entries.name: A tick that draws on
entries.line: Draws a round-capped tick mark stroke by stroke at a time, sized to what it sits on.
entries.use_for: done, passed, proven; the answer side of a tile; a checked row

call.signature: PCS.tick(comp, { size, color, t, dur, name })

options.name: size
options.text: width of the thing it sits on, default 82

options.name: color
options.text: default the style's colour for things on the accent

options.name: t
options.text: when it starts drawing (without t it is drawn from the start)

options.name: dur
options.text: seconds to draw, default 0.18

call.returns: the shape layer; seat it with PCS.onFace
call.example:
var tile = PCS.plate(st.comp, { name: 'tile', w: 300, h: 300, round: 56, color: PCS.S.accent, pos: [540, 600, 0] });
PCS.onFace(PCS.tick(st.comp, { size: 260, t: 1.0 }), tile);

entries.name: Tip an object away into the dark
entries.line: An object tips backward and falls away behind the backplate, then is hidden with what sits on it; type on it goes once it has tipped half way, so it is never seen squashed.
entries.use_for: dismissing what is finished as the next thing arrives; a wrong or hollow answer leaving (flag a problem with it); a line of words leaving; clearing the frame without a fade

call.signature: PCS.tipAway(plate, { t, dur, down, back })

options.name: t
options.text: when it starts (required)

options.name: dur
options.text: seconds, default 0.45

options.name: down
options.text: how far it drops, default 200

options.name: back
options.text: how far it travels back from the camera, default 800 (behind the backplate)

call.example:
var yes = PCS.type3d(st.comp, { text: 'Yes', size: 240, pos: [770, 640, 0] });
PCS.tipAway(yes, { t: 2.4 });
notes: it falls back, never down through the face card. Never fade or grey something out to dismiss it.

entries.name: One object with a different colour each side
entries.line: Makes one thick object whose front is one colour and whose back is another, so a flip changes its colour as well as what it says.
entries.use_for: a question that turns into the answer (a question mark on one side, the answer on the other); a question set against its answer; wrong to right; a quiet tile that turns to the accent

call.signature: PCS.twoSided(comp, { name, w, h, round, color, backColor, depth, bevel, pos, tilt, axis })

options.name: color
options.text: the front, default the style's surface

options.name: backColor
options.text: the back, default the style's quiet colour

options.name: axis
options.text: the axis it will flip on, 'y' (default) or 'x', so the back reads the right way up

options.name: w, h, round, depth, bevel, pos, tilt
options.text: as piece-plate

call.returns: { front, back }: move and flip front; seat things with PCS.onFace(layer, obj.front) and PCS.onFace(layer, obj.back)

entries.name: One hero word or number as a lit object
entries.line: Makes one word or number a solid, lit object with a shallow extrusion and no bevel, that casts a shadow and shows its side wall.
entries.use_for: a big word on its own (a yes, a no, a name) or a big number; the number the line lands on; the one word that is the answer; never a sentence

call.signature: PCS.type3d(comp, { text, size, depth, weight, color, pos, tilt, maxWidth, name })

options.name: text
options.text: the word or number

options.name: size
options.text: pixels, default 330

options.name: depth
options.text: extrusion, default 12 percent of the size

options.name: color
options.text: default the style's type colour; the face renders as that colour under the style's light (its typeLit)

options.name: pos
options.text: [x, y, z]

options.name: tilt
options.text: [x, y] resting angle, default the style's tilt

options.name: maxWidth
options.text: shrinks the size until it fits, default 860

call.example:
var n = PCS.type3d(st.comp, { text: '42', size: 420, pos: [540, 560, 0] });
PCS.label(st.comp, { text: 'tests passed', size: 64, pos: [540, 860, 0] });
notes: no bevel and a shallow depth: deeper or bevelled type reads as word art. Supporting words are piece-label.

its face is lit and set (the style's typeLit) to render as the cream type colour at rest in the middle and lower stage; near the top of the stage it reads a shade darker. Bring it in with piece-stand-up and take it off with piece-tip-away.

entries.name: A line that builds word by word
entries.line: Lays out one line of flat words and shows each at its own time; the words never slide, and the part already shown stays centred where you put the line (or under an object).
entries.use_for: a phrase whose words appear one at a time as they are said; a second message that builds on the back of a card after a flip

call.signature: PCS.words(comp, { words: [{ text, t }], size, weight, color, on, gap, name, pos, under, below, centre })

options.name: words
options.text: each { text, t }: the word and the time it appears (0 or no t: from the start)

options.name: size
options.text: pixels, default 64

options.name: on
options.text: 'ground' (default), 'surface' or 'accent', as piece-label

options.name: gap
options.text: space between words, default 0.28 of the size

options.name: pos
options.text: [x, y, z] where the line's centre sits (default [540, 960, 0]); graphics live in about y 220 to 1180

options.name: under
options.text: a layer to hang the line under, centred on it (instead of pos); below: space between its bottom edge and the line, default 0.9 of the size

options.name: centre
options.text: 'visible' (default) keeps the words shown so far centred, easing the line over by half a word as each one appears; 'line' lays the whole line out centred from the start, so the first words sit left of centre until it is complete

call.returns: { holder, layers, width }: the holder is a null the words hang on; move it with its moves (tip-away), or seat it on a face (PCS.onFace(line.holder, card))
notes: time each word to the voice; a word that slides in makes the whole line look like it moves.

entries.name: Overshoot bounce on a word's drop-in, with a second word staggered behind it
entries.line: Reach for it when a title or intro line needs words that snap in quickly, spring slightly past their rest spot, and swap out for the next word without a gap. It is a cheap way to get a lively, smooth text intro with only a few keys.

section.heading: Overshoot bounce on a word's drop-in, with a second word staggered behind it

entries.name: Concentric gradient discs from a Repeater with eased scale and rotation
entries.line: A calm, minimal animated backdrop for a title or explainer; it sits behind text that pops in with an overshoot bounce.

section.heading: Concentric gradient discs from a Repeater with eased scale and rotation

entries.name: Long soft shadow from a blacked-out copy and a radial blur
entries.line: Reach for it when a card, thumbnail or panel on a plain light ground needs to lift off the page with a long, soft, directional shadow, as a stronger and softer alternative to the stock drop shadow.

section.heading: Long soft shadow from a blacked-out copy and a radial blur

entries.name: Hand-traced script word that draws itself and glows
entries.line: A designer reaches for this when a short word (a greeting, a title) should look written by a glowing line on a dark ground.

section.heading: Hand-traced script word that draws itself and glows

entries.name: Frosted glass bar refracting a smeared gradient star
entries.line: A premium title or UI backdrop: a pill-shaped pane of frosted glass sits over a soft, flowing colour field and bends what lies behind it. Reach for it when text needs a rich, calm, frosted-glass ground.

section.heading: Frosted glass bar refracting a smeared gradient star

entries.name: Window-light shadow map over a flat layout
entries.line: Makes a flat title card or layout look as if it sits in a room with sunlight falling through a window: long soft diagonal shadows with light bands between them. Reach for it when a clean graphic looks too digital and needs contrast and a sense of place without any 3D.

section.heading: Window-light shadow map over a flat layout

entries.name: Soft diagonal wipe-on for a shadow map
entries.line: Brings window-light shadows into a shot as if the sun had just come out: the shadow sweeps across the layout along the strips over about a second instead of popping on. Use it on the opening beat of a title card that carries a shadow map.

section.heading: Soft diagonal wipe-on for a shadow map

entries.name: Graphics riding a spinning real object
entries.line: Lets a real photographed object drive the motion: a cut-out wheel (or any round object) spins, and a ring of graphic cards fanned around its centre turns with it like a carousel. Use it for a "meet the team" or product-range beat that should feel physical rather than a plain slider.

section.heading: Graphics riding a spinning real object

entries.name: Swap a layer's photo and keep everything built on it
entries.line: A time-saver, not a look. Once one card, slot or frame is fully built (transforms, masks or mattes, parenting, keyframes, effects), you put a different photo or clip into it without rebuilding anything.

section.heading: Swap a layer's photo and keep everything built on it

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Seat a cut-out object with a soft, doubled drop shadow
entries.line: When a photographed object cut out of its background (a product, a prop, a wheel) is dropped into a flat graphic scene and looks pasted on, a very soft, barely offset drop shadow gives it a dark halo that grounds it. Stack a second, even softer copy when the first is too faint.

section.heading: Seat a cut-out object with a soft, doubled drop shadow

entries.name: Tuck graphics behind a person with an automatic object matte
entries.line: For talking-head or presenter footage on a plain wall: cards, titles and text sit between the person and the wall, so the person stands in front of the graphics. Reach for it when overlays would otherwise cover the face or body.

section.heading: Tuck graphics behind a person with an automatic object matte

entries.name: Key a rough, unevenly lit green backdrop with a machine-learning keyer
entries.line: For stock or found footage shot against a coloured wall that was never meant to be keyed (uneven light, olive green, shadows), when a classic colour keyer leaves grey residue. The person comes out clean, hair included, ready to sit over graphics.

section.heading: Key a rough, unevenly lit green backdrop with a machine-learning keyer

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Stacked white discs that grow out of the centre with long soft shadows
entries.line: A title or opener background that makes a near-white frame look premium and tactile: white discs swell out from the centre one after another, each one raised off the one below with a pale rim and a long, soft shadow to one side. Reach for it when a clean white brand look needs depth and slow motion behind type.

section.heading: Stacked white discs that grow out of the centre with long soft shadows

entries.name: Soft lens blur at the frame sides plus fine grain
entries.line: A last pass that makes a clean, drawn graphic look as if it was shot through a lens: the left and right sides go slightly soft while the centre stays crisp, and a little grain breaks up the flat digital fills. Use it on any finished graphic or title plate, especially pale ones where the cleanliness gives away that they are drawn.

section.heading: Soft lens blur at the frame sides plus fine grain

entries.name: Flat UI graphic on a glossy extruded plate
entries.line: Turns a flat 2D card or UI panel into a solid, glossy object floating over a pale floor with a real cast shadow, while the graphic on its face keeps its exact flat colours. Reach for it when a 2D layout needs to read as a physical product shot without leaving After Effects.

section.heading: Flat UI graphic on a glossy extruded plate

entries.name: Depth of field on a row of glossy plates (Advanced 3D camera)
entries.line: Gives a 3D product-style scene a photographic lens: duplicated objects staggered in depth fall progressively out of focus, and a small camera move adds life. Use it to sell scale and depth once a scene from recipe 10 exists.

section.heading: Depth of field on a row of glossy plates (Advanced 3D camera)

entries.name: Soft one-way blurred dark shapes with a bright stroke fringe on a pale ground
entries.line: Turns two flat, crude shapes into a soft, lens-like backdrop in under a minute. Reach for it when a title or scene needs an organic, out-of-focus base layer rather than hard vector art.

section.heading: Soft one-way blurred dark shapes with a bright stroke fringe on a pale ground

entries.name: Wiggled glow, darkest radial blur and fine grain finish for bright scenes
entries.line: A three-adjustment-layer finish that makes any soft, light-backed composition bloom and gain film grit, with wiggle expressions on the glow radius and blur amount as its only source of movement. Use it over a blurred or abstract backdrop (in the tutorial, the blurred shapes of technique 01, whose figures are repeated in step 1) when the frame feels static and digital.

section.heading: Wiggled glow, darkest radial blur and fine grain finish for bright scenes

entries.name: Soft pockets of light from heavily blurred edge shapes
entries.line: Adds soft patches of lighter tone around the edges of an otherwise finished frame (with a wiggle on one blur for movement), so the dark areas are not flat and the eye is pulled toward the centre. A quick pass to make a background feel lit and alive.

section.heading: Soft pockets of light from heavily blurred edge shapes

entries.name: Liquid merge of outlined circles with blur and choke
entries.line: Makes separate shapes fuse like drops of liquid when one drifts into another, so a plain layout of circles becomes an organic, slow-breathing background or a morph between two forms.

section.heading: Liquid merge of outlined circles with blur and choke

entries.name: A dark mass split open behind a travelling ball
entries.line: A small ball crosses the frame and a large dark form tears open behind it, revealing the light ground; good for line-led animation, progress moments or a reveal that clears space for a headline.

section.heading: A dark mass split open behind a travelling ball

entries.name: Turning a crude gradient disc into a grainy glowing orb
entries.line: Rescues a deliberately plain graphic (two gradient circles) into a soft, filmic hero object for a title card or an event poster background, using only blur, heavy grain, a huge glow and posterize.

section.heading: Turning a crude gradient disc into a grainy glowing orb

entries.name: Slider-driven minutes:seconds countdown timer
entries.line: Put a live countdown clock (MM:SS) on screen when a scene needs a timer, a deadline or a ticking tension beat. Only one number is keyed, so the length is changed by editing two key values.

section.heading: Slider-driven minutes:seconds countdown timer

entries.name: Edge-only light outline from a solid logo
entries.line: Turn a solid-colour logo into a thin glowing rim line with nothing inside it, as the base for an animated outline reveal.

section.heading: Edge-only light outline from a solid logo

entries.name: Three coloured edge sweeps that spin in and meet at one angle
entries.line: Reveal a logo as thin bright outlines that start at different angles, race around it and lock together at one point. Use it when a logo needs a sleek outline intro before the fill or glow arrives.

section.heading: Three coloured edge sweeps that spin in and meet at one angle

entries.name: Four stacked Glow effects blooming a thin outline
entries.line: When a thin bright outline on black needs to read as lit from within, with a tight hot edge, a near halo and a wide soft haze. One Glow is flat; several at growing radii give the falloff.

section.heading: Four stacked Glow effects blooming a thin outline

entries.name: Animated light-sweep width: outline brightens, spreads, starts hidden
entries.line: Make a rim-lit logo come alive: the lit edges widen and brighten over the first seconds, and at the start nothing is visible, so the outline fades in while it keeps turning.

section.heading: Animated light-sweep width: outline brightens, spreads, starts hidden

entries.name: Solid logo fading in over a glowing outline, with a hot highlight and a small scale-down
entries.line: When a thin glowing outline logo should land as a finished, solid, clean logo: the outline's glow dies away, a flare flashes over the top of the shape, the solid fill fades in and the whole logo settles slightly smaller.

section.heading: Solid logo fading in over a glowing outline, with a hot highlight and a small scale-down

entries.name: Swap the logo or text inside a finished glow-reveal setup
entries.line: When a glowing outline-and-flash logo reveal is already built on a pre-composed logo, this reuses it for another mark or a word. Replace the artwork inside the pre-comp and the whole animation carries over unchanged.

section.heading: Swap the logo or text inside a finished glow-reveal setup

entries.name: Counter driven by one slider on a control null
entries.line: A stat that counts up (or down) to a figure, so a number lands with weight. The same slider later drives a ring (02-ring-fills-to-value) and bars (03-bars-grow-to-values), so one keyframed value moves the number and its graphic together.

section.heading: Counter driven by one slider on a control null

entries.name: Ring that fills to the counter's value
entries.line: A percentage stat shown as a donut that draws on to the same figure the number counts to, so the graphic and the number can never disagree. Builds on 01-value-driven-counter: it reuses that recipe's null and slider.

section.heading: Ring that fills to the counter's value

entries.name: Round-capped bars that grow to their own values
entries.line: A comparison beat: several figures rise side by side, each to its own value, so the viewer reads which is biggest. Builds on 01-value-driven-counter (a null whose sliders hold the values) and 02-ring-fills-to-value (dim track under a coloured copy, Trim Paths End linked to a slider).

section.heading: Round-capped bars that grow to their own values

entries.name: Icon that fills up to a value
entries.line: Turns a flat icon into a gauge: a bright copy of the icon rises from the bottom over a dim copy and stops at a figure, so a stat reads as "how full". Reach for it beside a counter when a percentage needs a picture.

section.heading: Icon that fills up to a value

entries.name: Map regions that fade up one by one
entries.line: Marks places on a map: chosen regions light up in colour over a grey base map, each with a numbered list entry, so a viewer reads "these places" in order. Use it for coverage, rankings or "where" beats.

section.heading: Map regions that fade up one by one

entries.name: Before/after reveal with a sliding rectangle matte and thin edge line
entries.line: Show the same subject before and after one change. The "after" picture sits over the "before" picture and is uncovered by a straight vertical edge that sweeps across and then back.

section.heading: Before/after reveal with a sliding rectangle matte and thin edge line

entries.name: A pill button built in its own comp
entries.line: The call-to-action button for an end card or app demo: a flat, fully rounded pill with a centred caps label, kept in its own comp so the scene can place, scale, slide and "press" it as one layer.

section.heading: A pill button built in its own comp

entries.name: A soft coloured lift under a button, and an inset label
entries.line: Lifts a flat UI button off a white page so it reads as a pressable object, with a long, very soft glow-like shadow in the button's own colour straight underneath, and gives the label a slight pressed-in feel with two tiny shadows.

section.heading: A soft coloured lift under a button, and an inset label

entries.name: Headline, button and web address stacked on a white square
entries.line: The closing card of a social ad or product promo: one line of headline, one button and a quiet web address, on a clean white square, centred on one vertical axis and ready to be animated in.

section.heading: Headline, button and web address stacked on a white square

entries.name: Tap cursor built from two translucent discs
entries.line: A stand-in for a finger or touch point in a UI demo. It is a soft, translucent touch marker that reads on a white screen without hiding the button under it.

section.heading: Tap cursor built from two translucent discs

entries.name: Card elements slide in from the left, one after another
entries.line: Builds an end card or call-to-action screen in a quick, readable cascade: each element arrives from off the left edge and lands in place a few frames after the one above it, so the eye reads headline, then button, then address.

section.heading: Card elements slide in from the left, one after another

entries.name: Cursor glides in and taps the button
entries.line: Shows a tap on a UI element. A touch marker slides in from off screen and stops on a button, and the button dips in scale and springs back, so the viewer reads "pressed".

section.heading: Cursor glides in and taps the button

entries.name: Curved, eased cursor route in and out
entries.line: Makes a touch marker move like a hand, not a robot. It arcs in, pauses on the button for the tap, then arcs out and off screen, with eased starts and stops.

section.heading: Curved, eased cursor route in and out

entries.name: Card elements slide out to the right in the same cascade
entries.line: Clears an end card or call-to-action screen with the same cascade it arrived with, carried on in the same direction: the elements leave off the right edge one after another, so the card reads as passing through the frame. Also a pass to even out the gaps between entrance, tap and exit.

section.heading: Card elements slide out to the right in the same cascade

entries.name: Round-capped line that draws on and then wipes off (Trim Paths)
entries.line: A designer reaches for this when a plain stroke should grow along its path and then have its tail chase the head off the far end, as a quick graphic accent or as the building block for a larger line design.

section.heading: Round-capped line that draws on and then wipes off (Trim Paths)

entries.name: Two travelling lines turned into an X by duplicating and rotating
entries.line: A designer reaches for this when one animated stroke (see recipe 01-trim-paths-travelling-round-cap-line) should become a symbol or accent such as a cross, a close mark or a plus-style hit, by reusing the same animation on turned copies.

section.heading: Two travelling lines turned into an X by duplicating and rotating

entries.name: Round dots from a shape stroke
entries.line: Turns any stroked line or outline into an evenly spaced row or ring of round dots with no extra layers, for loaders, orbit rings, borders and decorative circles around a title.

section.heading: Round dots from a shape stroke

entries.name: Arc with a dot at each end
entries.line: A thin line or arc with a round dot at each end, built inside one shape layer, for orbit segments, connector lines, data callouts and ring loaders.

section.heading: Arc with a dot at each end

entries.name: Fade both ends of an open stroke with Taper
entries.line: Makes an open stroke thin to nothing at both ends, so a light streak, horizon arc or swoosh fades out softly instead of stopping in a hard square end.

section.heading: Fade both ends of an open stroke with Taper

entries.name: Text carousel from rotated copies around one pivot
entries.line: Builds a wheel of repeated words (or any layer) curving around an off-screen pivot. Use it for list reveals, title wheels and "rolodex" type moments without expressions or plugins.

section.heading: Text carousel from rotated copies around one pivot

entries.name: Even time stagger by dragging a whole stack at once
entries.line: Makes a stack of copies appear one after another at an even interval, so items of a list, ring or grid arrive in sequence. A quick replacement for Sequence Layers or hand-nudging each bar.

section.heading: Even time stagger by dragging a whole stack at once

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Tilted 3D ring of discs orbiting a centre
entries.line: Wraps a central object in a tilted, torus-like ring of repeated flat shapes that pass in front of and behind it. Use it for an orbit or "planet with rings" look, or any hero object that needs a 3D halo, with no 3D plugin.

section.heading: Tilted 3D ring of discs orbiting a centre

entries.name: Keep an orbiting 3D layer turned towards the camera
entries.line: When a flat 3D layer circles around something (a moon round a planet, an icon on an orbit), it turns edge-on and thins out at parts of the loop; this keeps it reading as a full, flat shape the whole way round.

section.heading: Keep an orbiting 3D layer turned towards the camera

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Perform puppet-pin motion live with the mouse
entries.line: For organic secondary motion on an illustrated character (a head sway, a nod, a drifting limb) where hand-placing keyframes would look stiff or take too long; you act the motion out once and After Effects writes the keyframes.

section.heading: Perform puppet-pin motion live with the mouse

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Slide a background endlessly with mirrored tiling
entries.line: For a background that has to keep moving longer than the artwork is wide, such as the view out of a moving vehicle's window; the image is repeated and slid along without visible seams.

section.heading: Slide a background endlessly with mirrored tiling

entries.name: Leaf-shaped particles from any graphic
entries.line: Fill a scene with drifting copies of a small graphic (leaves, petals, confetti, logos) without hand-placing them; the particle system births, spins and moves each copy for you.

section.heading: Leaf-shaped particles from any graphic

entries.name: Soft embossed finish for white shapes on a pale background
entries.line: When a pure white shape or title vanishes into a light background, two layer styles give it a faint cool shading and a bright rim. On their own they only tint the shape; it reads as a raised, soft-plastic object once a long soft shadow lies under it and the shapes around it get the same treatment, so the pieces look stacked.

section.heading: Soft embossed finish for white shapes on a pale background

entries.name: Long soft shadow from a radially blurred black copy
entries.line: Gives flat shapes or letters a long, fading directional shadow, as if lit by a low sun, which reads especially well on bright, pale backgrounds.

section.heading: Long soft shadow from a radially blurred black copy

entries.name: Fine dot-grid background from a ball-grid effect
entries.line: A quick, quiet design texture for a plain or pale background, so an empty backdrop reads as designed rather than blank without pulling focus from the type or graphics in front.

section.heading: Fine dot-grid background from a ball-grid effect

entries.name: Real cast shadows on an invisible 3D floor
entries.line: Grounds flat 3D layers in a scene by giving them soft, believable shadows on the ground, without letting the light change the colour of the graphics themselves.

section.heading: Real cast shadows on an invisible 3D floor

entries.name: Un-clip an effect with Grow Bounds
entries.line: Fixes effects that are cut off with a hard edge because the layer's bounding box is too small, for example a blurred or stretched shadow running past the edge of its source artwork.

section.heading: Un-clip an effect with Grow Bounds

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Keep a chosen layer sharp while the camera travels
entries.line: Use when a camera push or drift through a layered 3D scene should keep the hero element crisp the whole time, so depth of field never drifts off the subject as the camera's distance to it changes.

section.heading: Keep a chosen layer sharp while the camera travels

entries.name: Tie a 3D scene together with depth fog over the precomp
entries.line: Use when separately made 3D layers look pasted together; a coloured depth fog over the finished scene lifts the darks and sinks the distance into one atmosphere.

section.heading: Tie a 3D scene together with depth fog over the precomp

entries.name: Soft word-by-word rise-and-fade text reveal
entries.line: Use for a headline or tagline that should arrive gently, words sliding up and fading in one after another with a smooth overlap, with no per-word keyframes.

section.heading: Soft word-by-word rise-and-fade text reveal

entries.name: Text that runs round a drawn path
entries.line: Wrap a repeated line of type round a circle (or any shape you draw) and slide it along the path, so a badge or seal of words circles a central title.

section.heading: Text that runs round a drawn path

entries.name: Two stacked glows for a soft cinematic bloom
entries.line: A finishing pass on bright line art or type on a dark ground: one tight glow for a halo near the edges plus one very wide glow for a faint bloom, without looking blown out.

section.heading: Two stacked glows for a soft cinematic bloom

entries.name: Paper texture through a title matte, with roughened edges
entries.line: Make a title look printed or stamped into a worn paper texture instead of floating on top of it: the texture itself forms the letters, brightened, and the letter edges are broken up.

section.heading: Paper texture through a title matte, with roughened edges

entries.name: Tuck helper layers out of the timeline with the shy switch
entries.line: When a comp has dozens of support layers (mattes, lines, labels) and you only want to touch a few, mark the rest shy and hide them from the layer stack without precomposing. The comp structure and the render stay unchanged.

section.heading: Tuck helper layers out of the timeline with the shy switch

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Dial motion blur strength with the comp's shutter angle
entries.line: When motion blur is on but reads too subtle (or too smeary), change the composition's shutter angle to set how long each frame's blur streak is, without touching the animation.

section.heading: Dial motion blur strength with the comp's shutter angle

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Keep a scaled-up precomp of vector art crisp
entries.line: When a precomp built from shape and text layers is pushed far past 100% (a big push-in or a hero zoom), turn on the layer's collapse/rasterize switch so the vector contents are redrawn at the new size instead of being enlarged as pixels.

section.heading: Keep a scaled-up precomp of vector art crisp

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Frame video in a custom shape with a track matte
entries.line: When a photo or clip should sit in a designed window rather than a plain rectangle (for example, a cut-out that leaves room for a headline), draw any shape and use it as the clip's matte.

section.heading: Frame video in a custom shape with a track matte

entries.name: Rounded-rectangle matte card that carries its media and labels
entries.line: Turns any photo or clip into a tidy rounded card whose size and position are driven by one shape layer, so the card can later be swung, scaled or duplicated as a unit. Reach for it as the base piece of any card carousel or media stack.

section.heading: Rounded-rectangle matte card that carries its media and labels

entries.name: Card that swings round a pivot below the frame, one step at a time, forever
entries.line: Gives a card (or later a row of cards) a carousel step: it swings in from one side on a big arc, settles upright, pauses, then swings out the other side, and the step repeats endlessly from only three keyframes. Use it for product or photo carousels, list reveals, or any "next item" rhythm.

section.heading: Card that swings round a pivot below the frame, one step at a time, forever

entries.name: Card shrinks and leans outward at the ends of its swing
entries.line: Adds a size-and-lean change on top of the pivot swing so the card is small and tipped outward while it is off to the side and full size and upright when it reaches the top. This is what makes a swinging carousel feel like it is "resizing" and gives the centred item its emphasis.

section.heading: Card shrinks and leans outward at the ends of its swing

entries.name: Chained copies of a swinging card, placed with a helper null
entries.line: Turns one looping swing card into a carousel of several cards that follow each other round the same pivot, one swing step apart, so a new card always arrives as the previous one leaves. Reach for it for product, photo or profile carousels where each beat shows the next item.

section.heading: Chained copies of a swinging card, placed with a helper null

entries.name: Cards orbiting an ellipse drawn as a mask
entries.line: Sends a ring of photo cards round an oval forever, framing a title or product in the middle. Use it for an endless moodboard or gallery loop behind a headline, or a hold that has to run for any length.

section.heading: Cards orbiting an ellipse drawn as a mask

entries.name: Cards growing along a drawn path into a stacked trail
entries.line: A stream of photo cards is born as specks, grows and straightens as it sweeps along a looping path, and brakes to a stop in a fanned stack. Use it for a gallery reveal, a "many stories" opener, or a build-up behind a title.

section.heading: Cards growing along a drawn path into a stacked trail

entries.name: Spinning square box built from four 3D cards
entries.line: Turns a handful of photo cards into a rotating four-walled box seen end-on, a quick 3D showcase loop for a gallery or "many images" moment, and the base unit for the tunnel in 08.

section.heading: Spinning square box built from four 3D cards

entries.name: Counter-spinning tunnel from stacked card boxes
entries.line: Extends the spinning box (07) into a deep tunnel of photo walls whose alternate rings turn in opposite directions; a hypnotic gallery loop or the set for a camera fly-through (09).

section.heading: Counter-spinning tunnel from stacked card boxes

entries.name: Camera push into the card tunnel with depth of field
entries.line: Flies the viewer into the counter-spinning card tunnel (08) while shallow focus melts the near and far walls, for an immersive opener or transition through a wall of images.

section.heading: Camera push into the card tunnel with depth of field

entries.name: Ring of 3D photo cards seen from inside
entries.line: Puts the viewer in the middle of a slowly turning ring of photo cards, so a gallery wraps around the frame instead of sliding past it. Reach for it for a portfolio, lookbook or "many stories" moment.

section.heading: Ring of 3D photo cards seen from inside

entries.name: Wide-lens camera inside the card ring
entries.line: A one-step finish for the ring of cards in 10-inner-ring-carousel: a short-focal-length camera stretches the perspective so the ring reads as a wide, immersive sweep rather than three flat cards. Use it whenever a 3D layout looks too flat under the default view.

section.heading: Wide-lens camera inside the card ring

entries.name: Fail, then fix: a red X on the wrong state, a wipe to the fixed one, a tick on the result
entries.line: Show something going wrong and then the fix making it right, as one beat: the wrong state is struck with a red X, a straight edge wipes the fixed state on over it and takes the X away, and a tick draws on the result.

section.heading: Fail, then fix: a red X on the wrong state, a wipe to the fixed one, a tick on the result

entries.name: Bevelled 3D text wrapped in a tiled material
entries.line: Turns a flat title into a solid, physical object with rounded edges and a real surface (metal, stone, paint) in a few clicks; the base for any lit 3D title shot.

section.heading: Bevelled 3D text wrapped in a tiled material

entries.name: Backlit environment light over a shadow-only floor
entries.line: The quick way to make a textured 3D title look photographed rather than flat: one environment light turned round behind the text so long soft shadows fall toward the viewer onto an invisible floor, with a slow light swing for movement.

section.heading: Backlit environment light over a shadow-only floor

entries.name: Shadowless parallel light as an extra backlight
entries.line: A small finishing touch on a lit 3D title: a second, shadowless directional light from behind and to one side brightens the edges and tops of the letters without adding a second set of shadows.

section.heading: Shadowless parallel light as an extra backlight

entries.name: Soft front fill from a point light with smooth falloff
entries.line: Reach for this when lit 3D type reads as one flat wash from the front; a small, soft pool of light off to one side gives the faces a gentle gradient so the letters stop looking evenly lit.

section.heading: Soft front fill from a point light with smooth falloff

entries.name: Letters tumble in from just in front of the lens, one after another
entries.line: A smooth, weighty title entrance for extruded 3D type: each letter starts turned and in front of the lens, then swings into place in a rolling wave, so the word assembles itself without any hard pop.

section.heading: Letters tumble in from just in front of the lens, one after another

entries.name: Depth-of-field camera on a null, pushed in through the shot
entries.line: Add this on top of a 3D type entrance to make it feel filmed: letters close to the lens go soft, and a slow camera push keeps the frame alive after the word has landed.

section.heading: Depth-of-field camera on a null, pushed in through the shot

entries.name: Warm-sided metal title: textured faces, plain tinted sides
entries.line: A fast restyle of an already-built textured 3D title when you want a warmer, more polished metal read without rebuilding the material: keep the texture only where it matters and let the extruded sides catch light as a tinted metal.

section.heading: Warm-sided metal title: textured faces, plain tinted sides

entries.name: Hollow chrome outline title: faces hidden, bevels and walls remain
entries.line: A cut-out, stroke-like 3D title for a sleek or dark mood: the letter faces vanish and only the rounded bevels and the extrusion walls remain, so the word reads as a hollow metal outline standing on a floor.

section.heading: Hollow chrome outline title: faces hidden, bevels and walls remain

entries.name: Spinning ring of standing 3D letters, stackable
entries.line: A seamless looping title or bumper: a word repeated around a circle stands up like a carousel and turns forever, and stacked copies make a tower of rings; good for intros, loops and background type.

section.heading: Spinning ring of standing 3D letters, stackable

entries.name: Found vector art, one object per file, laid out as separate layers
entries.line: The groundwork for a lit, deep 2D scene when you cannot draw: gather ready-made vector illustrations, keep only the pieces you need, and bring every object into After Effects as its own layer so each one can later be graded and placed in depth on its own. Assumes: nothing; it starts from an empty project.

section.heading: Found vector art, one object per file, laid out as separate layers

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: One mood grade for mismatched art: Tritone plus a single-point Curves, pasted to every layer
entries.line: When a scene is built from stock pieces that do not match (saturated greens, different palettes), this pulls them into one night-time or moody colour world in a minute, before any lighting or depth work. Assumes: a composition in which every scene object is its own layer (technique 01).

section.heading: One mood grade for mismatched art: Tritone plus a single-point Curves, pasted to every layer

entries.name: Flat cut-outs into a deep stage: push far layers back in Z, pull near ones forward, rescale to frame
entries.line: Sets up real parallax and depth of field for a 2D illustrated scene: the picture through the default view barely changes, but layers now sit thousands of pixels apart, so any later camera move or focus pull separates them. Assumes: the scene is already split into one layer per object (technique 01) and graded (technique 02), with Tritone switched off on the stone-wall layer so its lamp glows warm (off).

section.heading: Flat cut-outs into a deep stage: push far layers back in Z, pull near ones forward, rescale to frame

entries.name: Depth-of-field camera locked on the subject, with a slow dolly in
entries.line: Turns a staged 2D-in-3D layout into a filmed shot: near and far layers fall out of focus, the subject stays sharp, and a short push-in gives the opening beat life without any layer being animated.

section.heading: Depth-of-field camera locked on the subject, with a slow dolly in

entries.name: Endless wind sway from two rotation keys and a ping-pong loop
entries.line: Gives a still illustrated scene a reason to move (wind) with almost no keyframing: each branch or tree rocks back and forth forever from just two keys.

section.heading: Endless wind sway from two rotation keys and a ping-pong loop

entries.name: Grass rippling in the wind with Wave Warp
entries.line: Makes a field of many thin blades (grass, reeds, fur-like edges) move in the wind without animating a single blade: one effect, one setting, and it moves on its own.

section.heading: Grass rippling in the wind with Wave Warp

entries.name: Leaves blown across the frame with textured particles
entries.line: Sells wind in an illustrated scene by sending a steady trickle of tumbling leaves across it from one side, without animating a single leaf by hand. Assumes a finished, graded 2D scene in a 3D comp with a camera (techniques 02–04) and the scene's Tritone plus Curves grade on a layer to copy from.

section.heading: Leaves blown across the frame with textured particles

entries.name: Rain slanted to match the wind
entries.line: Adds weather on top of a wind-animated scene so the motion has a reason, with the rain leaning the same way everything else is blowing. Assumes a scene that already moves in one wind direction (techniques 05–07; here the leaves enter from the left edge).

section.heading: Rain slanted to match the wind

entries.name: Film-stock grain and mood finish on a top adjustment layer
entries.line: The last pass on an illustrated shot: real-film grain, one last overall curve, and an optional posterize for a rougher look, all in one layer over everything. Assumes the full scene is built beneath (techniques 01–09).

section.heading: Film-stock grain and mood finish on a top adjustment layer

entries.name: Long-lens close-up that matches the wide shot
entries.line: Assumes a finished wide scene already exists with separate 2D layers, a cold grade on each (Tritone + Curves, technique 02), a 3D camera with depth of field (04), sway on trees (05), rain and finishing adjustment layers (08, 10). Cut from an established wide scene to a close-up of the character without building a new world: reuse the wide shot's backdrop pieces, camera and finishing layers, and push the backdrop very deep so the close-up reads as shot on a long lens.

section.heading: Long-lens close-up that matches the wide shot

entries.no_still: unmatched: fits no job yet, so no proof still

entries.name: Side-light a face with a matted Curves layer
entries.line: Assumes a close-up with the character on its own layer (or pre-comp) under a scene grade (techniques 11 and 12). Adds a soft wash of differently coloured light to one side of the face and hair only, so a flat close-up gains a light direction without touching the background.

section.heading: Side-light a face with a matted Curves layer

entries.name: Two-colour phase bar that draws on segment after segment
entries.line: A process or timeline beat ("first this phase, then that one"): one straight bar split into coloured phases that fill left to right, the second phase starting just as the first slows down, with step pictures lined up underneath.

section.heading: Two-colour phase bar that draws on segment after segment

entries.name: Labels that rise out of their own bar segment
entries.line: Names each phase of a progress bar as that phase fills: the word slides up out of the bar as if it was tucked behind it, timed to its segment.

section.heading: Labels that rise out of their own bar segment

entries.name: Step pictures that pop in one after another with a small bounce
entries.line: Brings in a row of step pictures under a timeline one by one, each growing from nothing with a slight overshoot and settle, so the eye walks the process left to right.

section.heading: Step pictures that pop in one after another with a small bounce

entries.name: Small swept-head arrow that draws itself between steps
entries.line: Ties a row of step images into a process: a tiny arrow draws itself between each pair just as the next step appears, so the eye is led left to right one step at a time.

section.heading: Small swept-head arrow that draws itself between steps

entries.name: Stepped jitter and black-and-white photos for a hand-made finish
entries.line: Takes a clean, flat infographic and gives it a cut-out, stop-motion feel: photos go monochrome, each one twitches on its own a few times a second, the whole frame shakes slightly and all motion steps at a low frame rate. Reach for it when a data beat looks too slick or digital.

section.heading: Stepped jitter and black-and-white photos for a hand-made finish

entries.name: Faint graph-paper backdrop
entries.line: Swaps a plain black ground for an off-white sheet ruled with tiny pale-blue squares, like school exercise paper, so a flat infographic reads as hand-made and educational rather than digital.

section.heading: Faint graph-paper backdrop

entries.name: Bar chart of thick strokes that grow up in a ladder, with value labels sliding in beside them
entries.line: A quick "how big is each one" moment: four bars rise one after another from a shared baseline, left to right, tallest first, while each value label slides in from the left. Use it when a narrated figure needs a chart that builds as the voice lists the numbers.

section.heading: Bar chart of thick strokes that grow up in a ladder, with value labels sliding in beside them

entries.name: Chart baseline that draws outward from its middle
entries.line: Opens a chart (or any divider) with a line that grows out to both ends at once from its centre, a calm, balanced first move before the data arrives.

section.heading: Chart baseline that draws outward from its middle

entries.name: Faint grid held inside the chart's box, and the whole chart stepped to 12 fps
entries.line: Gives a bar chart a quiet graph-paper backing that stops at the chart's edges, and a slightly hand-made, stepped motion, so a plain data beat reads as designed rather than default.

section.heading: Faint grid held inside the chart's box, and the whole chart stepped to 12 fps

entries.name: Pie chart from one fat stroke, with the share pushed out
entries.line: A single-statistic beat ("X % of all ..."): a pie sweeps round from twelve o'clock, then the highlighted share slides out from the centre so the number has a piece to point at.

section.heading: Pie chart from one fat stroke, with the share pushed out

entries.name: Value label that rises in one word at a time
entries.line: Puts a short stat sentence next to a chart's highlighted piece ("18% of all ..."). The words pop up one after another two frames apart, so the line reads as it lands.

section.heading: Value label that rises in one word at a time

entries.name: Photo pyramid that dips, then splits into tiers to reveal labels
entries.line: A hierarchy or "levels" beat. A real-looking pyramid sits whole, gathers itself, then pulls apart into three tiers, and a label appears in each opening gap.

section.heading: Photo pyramid that dips, then splits into tiers to reveal labels

entries.name: Cut mid-move to a close-up, carried by a shared upward drift
entries.line: Moves from an overview to a detail without a visible transition. At the fastest moment of an animation, the shot cuts to a doubled-size view of the same animation. Both shots drift upward through the cut, so the eye reads one continuous move. A later slide down then visits the next detail.

section.heading: Cut mid-move to a close-up, carried by a shared upward drift

entries.name: Pinned instant photos swaying on a grey map
entries.line: Marks a few places on a map with small pinned instant photos that hang and sway a little, so a travel or "where it happened" beat feels hand-made and alive while the camera holds or moves over it.

section.heading: Pinned instant photos swaying on a grey map

entries.name: Ink-blend place highlights and a self-drawing border on a grey map
entries.line: Points at a region on an old map with soft coloured blobs that look printed into the paper, and draws a country's outline on cue, for "here is where it happened" beats in a travel or history piece.

section.heading: Ink-blend place highlights and a self-drawing border on a grey map

entries.name: Glossy red pill button that swings up from below in 3D
entries.line: A hook moment where a call-to-action button should arrive as a big event rather than just fade or pop. The button comes up from below, near the camera and tipped back, and settles flat in the middle.

section.heading: Glossy red pill button that swings up from below in 3D

entries.name: Overshoot-bounce pop-in for an icon, with a letter-by-letter text rise
entries.line: Reach for it when a button, icon or label should land with a springy settle instead of a flat scale-up, and when its words should rise in one letter after another.

section.heading: Overshoot-bounce pop-in for an icon, with a letter-by-letter text rise

entries.name: Glowing blue gradient line that draws on from a button
entries.line: Reach for it when a button or card needs a connector that grows out of it towards the next idea, with a neon look that stays soft rather than harsh. The curve is drawn with the pen tool, coloured with a multi-stop gradient stroke, lit with stacked built-in Glows and revealed with Trim Paths.

section.heading: Glowing blue gradient line that draws on from a button

entries.name: Moving edge highlight and liquid bounce on a glass button
entries.line: Reach for it when a dark rounded button or label card needs a rim of light where a glowing line meets it, and a springy pop-in that also squeezes sideways. Cheap way to make UI cards feel glassy and alive.

section.heading: Moving edge highlight and liquid bounce on a glass button

entries.name: Duplicate, mirror and stagger a button-and-line layout
entries.line: Turn one glowing button with a curved line into a branching diagram (two columns, two rows) and then retime it so each piece starts before the previous one has finished, all riding on one parent null that scrolls the view.

section.heading: Duplicate, mirror and stagger a button-and-line layout

entries.name: Faint ghost label with reversed gradient overlay, plus a vignette finish layer
entries.line: Reach for it when a button or card shows one word and you want a dim, secondary word hovering beneath it (a "what's happening" hint) that fades off instead of competing, then close the scene with a top adjustment layer carrying a vignette.

section.heading: Faint ghost label with reversed gradient overlay, plus a vignette finish layer

entries.name: Four buttons slide together and melt into one large app-window card
entries.line: Use it when a scene of several rounded buttons or cards must turn into one large panel (a notes or dashboard window) without a visible cut. A match cut hides the swap.

section.heading: Four buttons slide together and melt into one large app-window card

entries.name: Three popping window dots and a faint feathered grid inside a card
entries.line: Turns a plain rounded card into an app window: three coloured dots pop in at the top-left with a springy overshoot, and a very light grid sits behind the content, fading out towards the edges.

section.heading: Three popping window dots and a faint feathered grid inside a card

entries.name: Typed-on note text that deletes and retypes, with word-by-word fade and a hold-key camera push
entries.line: Reach for it when a fake notes or chat window needs its text to appear as if someone is writing it, changing their mind and retyping, and then the shot needs a little extra life so the held text is not static.

section.heading: Typed-on note text that deletes and retypes, with word-by-word fade and a hold-key camera push

entries.name: Glowing liquid orb from blurred wiggling shapes and a sphere
entries.line: A designer reaches for this when a voice or AI assistant needs a living, colourful, soft-lit ball that can pop up from a small dot, wobble and pulse while it "speaks".

section.heading: Glowing liquid orb from blurred wiggling shapes and a sphere

entries.name: Grow an orb out of a small dot through a chain of linked nulls
entries.line: Use it when a pre-made glowing orb has to appear from a tiny marker already on screen and then swell to fill the frame, while its position and size keep moving without a jump.

section.heading: Grow an orb out of a small dot through a chain of linked nulls

entries.name: Hollow glowing ring from a filled orb: inverted-matte cut-out, soft blur, then echo trails
entries.line: Reach for it when a soft glowing orb needs to become a thin outline so a headline can sit in its middle, and the outline should then multiply into a few lagging copies as it appears.

section.heading: Hollow glowing ring from a filled orb: inverted-matte cut-out, soft blur, then echo trails

entries.name: Caption that fades in dim, fills to full word by word, sharpens from a blur and keeps growing
entries.line: Closing caption for a hero graphic. The words are readable only as a faint ghost at first, then light up one word at a time while the block sharpens and slowly swells, so the shot never stops moving.

section.heading: Caption that fades in dim, fills to full word by word, sharpens from a blur and keeps growing

entries.name: Frosted-glass pill built from three stacked shape layers
entries.line: Reach for it when a card, banner or notification has to sit in front of a busy picture and look like frosted glass: it blurs whatever is behind it and gets a faint tint and a thin light outline. It is the base card that later techniques animate.

section.heading: Frosted-glass pill built from three stacked shape layers

entries.name: Null hierarchy: three group nulls under one master null
entries.line: Reach for it before animating a card made of many layers (shapes, text, logo). Each part-group gets its own null, and one master null sits above them, so the whole card or any single group moves with one layer.

section.heading: Null hierarchy: three group nulls under one master null

entries.no_still: build aid: serves no beat, so no proof still

entries.name: Two-key drop-in that settles with an expression bounce
entries.line: Reach for it when a card or group should drop into place and wobble a little before it rests, without hand-keying the overshoot. Two plain keys give the move; one pasted expression adds the settle on Position and on Scale.

section.heading: Two-key drop-in that settles with an expression bounce

entries.name: Offset the logo and text groups a few frames behind the card
entries.line: Reach for it when several parts of one card all get the same drop-and-settle move and read as a single stiff block. Sliding the start of each part a couple of frames later makes the parts land one after another.

section.heading: Offset the logo and text groups a few frames behind the card

entries.name: Second notification arrives and the first one is pushed back
entries.line: Use it when a second card lands on top of a card already on screen and the first should react: sink, shrink and settle with a small springy wobble instead of just being covered.
